summary: Montezuma County tower site at 11,620 ft in the San Juan National Forest; the register says it was taken down, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower has been taken down; the Colorado list marks it Removed with type Unknown; no removal date given

events.note: Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 18, 2009

evidence.quote: This tower has been taken down.

evidence.supports: Administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Colorado list: type Unknown, Removed, FFLOS US 534, CO 6
evidence.quote: Burro Peak Montezuma 37.48583 -108.10583 Unknown Removed FFLOS US 534, CO 6

evidence.supports: Second list (Forest Lookouts) labels this Montezuma County, San Juan National Forest lookout Burro Mountain, marked Removed
evidence.quote: BURRO MOUNTAIN Montezuma County San Juan National Forest Removed

evidence.supports: Montezuma and San Juan forests consolidated in 1947
evidence.quote: In 1947 the Montezuma and San Juan were consolidated

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the site a tower ('This tower has been taken down.'), while the Colorado list records its type as Unknown. The story says tower only where the register does.

sources.title: Burro Peak Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

sources.title: Administering the National Forests of Colorado (inventory 7)

notes_for_editor: Only three thin sources; no build year, design, staffing or fire history in any page I could open, so the story leaves those out. Search summaries (not opened, not used) point to a firelookout.org/cohost-co/burro.html entry that gives a 1910s build, a 1914 photo and an Old Montezuma National Forest label; that page returns 404 in the cache under both http and https, so verify it before adding any build detail. The 1947 forest consolidation sentence (source 4) is context only; no source ties this lookout to the old Montezuma forest. Brief elevation (3541.8 m) and coordinates match the register.
